_note: US capital requirements on the Standardized approach, the requirement the Federal Reserve publishes and the ratio the US extractor reads (bankcredit/extract/us.py). No US filing states an overall capital requirement, so it is built here: for a holding company, the minimum (CET1 4.5, Tier 1 6, total 8) plus its stress capital buffer and GSIB surcharge, which together form its Standardized approach capital conservation buffer (12 CFR 217.11(c)); the countercyclical buffer is 0 in the US. For an insured bank subsidiary, the minimum plus the fixed 2.5 capital conservation buffer (12 CFR 3.11 for national banks, 217.11 for state member banks; 324.11 would apply to a state nonmember bank and none is held). Each entity lists its periods oldest first; a period holds from its effective date until the next. The SCBs effective 1 October 2025 were kept unchanged for 2026 (Board vote, 4 February 2026; Large Bank Capital Requirements, June 2026), so no requirement effective 1 October 2026 exists. The GSIB surcharge is reset each 1 January: the June 2026 table gives those in effect from 1 January 2026, where only Goldman Sachs's changed (3.0 to 3.5). Checked 4 November 2026 against the Fed tables cited.
